input.question: Broad topic: history of India. Please recommend a comprehensive book that covers it from ancient times to 20th century.
input.ground_truth: Hate to harp on what you've already acknowledged, but South Asia is a very large, culturally/linguistically diverse area that is one of the earliest sites of civilization. Any one book you read is going to leave out a whole lot. It might be better to pick a particular region or time period or cultural phenomena/group that interests you, and then look for a book from there. That said, these are the three that I would recommend: 1) Early India, from Origins to AD 1300 (Romila Thapar) 2) India Before Europe (Catherine Asher & Cynthia Talbot) 3) A Concise History of Modern India (Metcalfe & Metcalfe)

Okay! Imagine you want to learn about a big, beautiful story about a country called India, from when it was very, very old (like, when people rode on elephants and wrote on stone) all the way up to the time when people had cars and airplanes (that’s the 20th century).

One really good book that tells this whole story is called **"India: A History" by John Keay**. But it’s a bit long for a 5-year-old, so maybe grown-ups or older kids read it.

If you want a book that’s easier to read and still tells the big story, you could try **"The History of India for Kids" by Radha Kumar**. This book uses lots of pictures and simple words to tell you about kings, queens, temples, and how India changed over time.

So, if you want to know everything about India’s story, from the very beginning to the time when people watched TV and used computers, these books can help you!
